newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan makes largest drug seizure in its history.
newsitem.headline: Jordan makes largest drug seizure in its history.

text.p: Jordanian police seized 31 kg (68 lb) of heroin and 16 kg (35 lb) of opium in transit from Turkey to a neigbouring Arab state in the largest bust in the country's history, officials said on Wednesday.
Colonel Maan Sharaida, head of the anti-narcotics division, said the bust in which the five-member gang involved were arrested "was the biggest amount seized in Jordan's history".

It followed two months of intelligence work after Jordanian officers were tipped by a Turkish informer with the help of anti-drug agencies in neighbouring Arab and foreign countries, Sharaida said, without elaborating.

The drugs, with a market value of $8.5 million, had recently been smuggled to Jordan across the Syrian border post of Ramtha for temporary storage on the way to re-export to a neigbouring undisclosed country, he said.
Sharaida said the gang of non-Jordanian Arab and foreign nationalities were arrested in Amman while preparing the cargo, hidden in the tank of a car with a foreign number plate.

"We in Jordan are starting to feel drug smugglers are starting to think of using Jordan to store drugs for smuggling to other areas..we will not allow them to use Jordan as a base to other countries," Sharaida told reporters.
The gang confessed to being members of a highly sophisticated drug cartel based in Turkey, employing the latest high-tech equipment, he added.
Jordan is a key route for drugs being smuggled via Turkey to Gulf states.
